name: Brooklyn Bridge Automated Pedestrian Counts Demonstration Project (Historic)
description:
This dataset contains hourly automated pedestrian counts recorded on the Brooklyn Bridge, capturing foot traffic in both directions: toward Manhattan and toward Brooklyn. Each row represents one hour at a given location, with the hour_beginning timestamp, location name, total pedestrian count, and directional counts. The data also includes weather conditions at the time of counting, such as a weather summary, temperature, and precipitation, along with latitude and longitude coordinates and a geocoded column for mapping. An events field notes any special events that may have affected traffic.

Because it combines pedestrian volumes with weather and event information over time, the dataset supports analyses of how weather, time of day, and special events influence bridge foot traffic. It could be used for transportation planning, crowd management, tourism research, or studies of pedestrian behavior, as well as for building visualizations or forecasting models of bridge usage.
